##### SUMMARY
<!--- Describe the change below, including rationale and design decisions -->
<!--- HINT: Include "Fixes #nnn" if you are fixing an existing issue -->
When using the `healthcheck`-parameter `start_period` the task will always be reported as changed. This was due to a bug where `StartPeriod` was not properly mapped against `start_period`. This PR fixes this issue.

I also found that the version check of `healthcheck.start_period` is wrong. `Healthcheck.StartPeriod` was introduced in in [1.29](https://docs.docker.com/engine/api/version-history/#v129-api-changes) and not 1.25.

Fixes #66146

##### ISSUE TYPE
<!--- Pick one below and delete the rest -->
- Bugfix Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
<!--- Write the short name of the module, plugin, task or feature below -->
docker_swarm_service

review_comments: Are you sure about the 2.6.0 change? According to the changelog (https://docker-py.readthedocs.io/en/stable/change-log.html) for 2.4.0, `Added support for start_period configuration in docker.types.Healthcheck.`.

Hmm yes that looks wrong. I changed it to align with the main `healthcheck` param which is marked as docker-py 2.6.0 https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/77f3babc7d0da631a73dd8a72c456d10d8098ef0/lib/ansible/modules/cloud/docker/docker_swarm_service.py#L2868

I need to look into if that’s not the right version.

Ah, ok. In that case 2.6.0 seems to be ok; the 2.6.0 changelog actually mentions: `Added support for the following parameters when creating a ContainerSpec object: groups, open_stdin, read_only, stop_signal, helathcheck, hosts, ns_config, configs, privileges.`

I guess `docker.types.Healthcheck` can only be used with regular containers in 2.4.0 then.
